description: A `risky(n)?` arm of a `return match …` propagates: the error reaches the caller's `!{}` (`boom:neg`), and the success value is the return value (`ok=4`).
rationale: §19.5.1 makes `expr?` an expression and so an `arm-body` (§18.2); §19.5.2: on an error "`?` causes the enclosing function to return that error variant immediately", on success it "unwraps it and produces the success value". In `return match …` the match's value IS the function's return, so both halves hold. impl#1 emitted the `?` literally (E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC — dpa-068 D4).
